title: Acceptance criterion for the guess-and-run machine
statement: Let $P$ and $Q$ be deterministic machines with Boolean work tapes, state sets $SP$ and $SQ$, and let $pexit$ be a state of $P$, $j$ a work-tape index, and $qentry$, $acc$, and $rej$ states of $Q$. Fix a finite Boolean input $z$, a time $TP$, and a configuration $cP$ such that running $P$ from its initial configuration on $z$ for $TP$ steps yields $cP$, whose state is $pexit$, and no earlier configuration has state $pexit$. Suppose that, for some natural number $m$, the $m$ cells starting at the head position of tape $j$ in $cP$ are all nonblank, the next cell is blank, and the cell immediately to their left is blank. Let $T$ be a natural number such that for every Boolean word $s$ of length $m$, machine $Q$, started in state $qentry$ with $s$ written on tape $j$ as prescribed by the guessed-run construction, reaches either $acc$ or $rej$ within some time $TQ\le T$, and reaches neither verdict at any earlier time. For every natural number $B$ with $TP+2m+T+11\le B$, there is a choice word of length $B$ that makes the guess-and-run machine halt with output $[\mathrm{true}]$ if and only if there is a Boolean word $s$ of length $m$ and a time $TQ$ at which $Q$ reaches $acc$, reaches neither $acc$ nor $rej$ earlier, and has empty output at time $TQ$.
